newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end weaker as caution rules market.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end weaker as caution rules market.

text.p: Caution was the watchword on the South African stock market on Wednesday, as shares clung to weaker levels after earlier being knocked down by futures trading.
Dealers said players were nervous of being caught offsides by futures arbitreurs, who have been blamed for the volatile dealings on the bourse this week.
Better-than-expected half-year results from heavyweight stock SAB, released around 1230 GMT, briefly helped the market off its lows, they said.
But shares soon swivelled lower again, depressed further by the rand losing its nerve and returning to overnight levels after initially striding firmer.
At the close the industrial index was 16.1 points weaker at 7,914.1 pushing the overall index down to 6,755.3 -- off 7.3 points on the day.
On the gold board shares spent a lifeless day hovering just above opening levels as bullion clung to the around the $382 level. The index finished up 10.3 points at 1,711.9.
